stem.en: A farmer keeps ₹20,000 aside for seeds and medicine, and may need it in any week of the year. Which place fits this money's time horizon and its need for cash?

text.en: A fifteen-year deposit, because a longer period earns the highest return of the four places.
Shares, because they can always be sold on the market on any morning the money is wanted.
A five-year bond, because it pays a steady interest every year until the money is needed.
A savings account, because it can be turned into cash on the same day the need arises.

explanation.en: Money that may be needed in any week has a time horizon of nearly zero, so liquidity decides the choice. A savings account gives cash the same day, while a deposit, a bond or shares may cost time or value when sold early.

hints.en: Start with the horizon, not the return. How much warning will the farmer have before he needs this money?
Which of the four places gives him the full amount in cash on the day he asks for it, with no price to negotiate?
